record.paper_title: Positive and free boundary solutions to singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption: an overview and open problems
record.original_question: For the compact-support solutions associated with problem (III), namely -Δu = K(x)(λu^β - u^α) in Ω with K(x)=1/d(x)^k, 0 < k < 2, and 0 < α < β < 1, what is the structure of the set of compact-support solutions?

evidence.quote: Now we study the problem -Δu = K(x)(λu^β-u^α) in Ω, u=0 on ∂Ω, with K(x)=1/d(x)^k with 0<k<2 and 0<α<β<1.
Information on the structure of the set of compact support solutions is interesting as well.

artifact.status_search_result: No specific results found addressing the structural classification of compact-support solutions for this singular sublinear absorption problem with weight 1/d(x)^k. The question appears to remain open.
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, and let $d(x) = \mathrm{dist}(x, \partial\Omega)$ denote the distance to the boundary. Fix parameters $0 < k < 2$, $0 < \alpha < \beta < 1$, and $\lambda > 0$, and define the weight $K(x) = 1/d(x)^k$. Consider the singular nonlinear elliptic Dirichlet problem
$$-\Delta u = K(x)\bigl(\lambda u^{\beta} - u^{\alpha}\bigr) \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u \geq 0 \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega.$$
A nonnegative solution $u$ is said to have compact support if the set $\{x \in \Omega : u(x) > 0\}$ is compactly contained in $\Omega$. Determine the structure of the set
$$\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cs}} = \{ u : u \text{ is a compact-support solution of the above problem}\}.$$
Specifically, describe its cardinality, topological structure (e.g., as a continuum or branch parameterized by $\lambda$), the geometry of the supports of its elements (uniqueness up to translation, multiplicity, layered/dead-core structure), and the dependence of these features on the parameters $\lambda$, $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $k$.
